title: Pai Hwai
text:
Mingalabar! My name is Pai but i go by Reina. I’m from Myanmar and my family is from the Mergui Islands. I love the sea and my favorite food is clam soup.
Before this program, I completed my bachelors in Singapore and worked at a bank in an analyst role. Before continuing my career in data, I chose this opportunity to study at UBC to deepen my technical skills and learn how to be better in data roles.
It’s my first time living in Canada, and I’m really excited to see snow for the first time. Before you go, please say hi to my furball Kailan. He’s the cutest little pomsky named after a vegtable.
To learn more about Quarto websites visit https://quarto.org/docs/websites.

title: My first weeks in MDS
text:
A quiet afternoon on the UBC campus.


The first week was exciting yet full of challenges. Navigating where classes are and understanding how to retrieve and submit assignments were the most difficult parts. The pace was fast but I think by mid week two, I was able to adjust my time management. I have a good idea now on where I should be putting in more work to cover all the concepts. I also found some nice study spots in the koerner library where it’s really quiet. UBC is a big campus and there are still so many places to explore. Some of my favorite scenic places has to be the water fountain. I also like to grab coffee and some snacks in between lectures and enjoy the seasonal drinks. It’s a little self reward system that gives me something to look forward to in the day. It’s started to be a little chilly in the mornings and I caught a small cold. But as we are settling into new routines, I am really happy to be studying at such a beautiful campus. The rain hasn’t caught up to us yet, so its a great weather to be out and about.

title: About Me
text: I grew up in Myanmar and Thailand before moving abroad to pursue my bachelor’s degree in Data Science at James Cook University Singapore. Singapore shaped me as a person as I was leaving a collectivist culture into a more independent one. I made good friends, attended conferences and took part in data competitions. After university, working in banking taught me alot about the impact of finance and the importance of building good human relationships. Beyond my career, I also got my real estate license and worked as an independent real estate agent on the side. When the inflation crisis hit in Myanmar, what I learned about finance and investing became especially valuable, as I was able to help my family manage our finances through more strategic investments.

title: About Me
text:
Why Data
My passion in data led to me to this program. Choosing big data as a career has its fair share of challenges. There is a persistent need to upskill to keep up with real-time demands. I think of data as the infrastructure powering the front lines of innovation. Seeing different industries through the lens of data is insightful, fascinating and impactful. Working with data taught me to think more analytically and it has been a rewarding experience to continue learning and growing in this field.

title: About Me
text:
Life Besides Data
Outside of Data Science, I enjoy cooking and learning about buddhist philosophies. I’ve recently methodized grocery shopping based off universal pantry staples, staples based off cuisine, and niche ingredients for different recipes. Good food is the cure to almost everything, I believe. I grew up with mostly asian flavors and cusines and they are a great comfort meal for whenever I’m feeling homesick. Cooking at home is also more nutritious. I’ve been learning more about medicinal ingredients and sharing my findings with my mom back home. On the weekends I like to plan for recipes and make my own versions. When the day ends, I like to medidate before going to bed. I think alot about inner peace, compassion and human sufferings. As I’ve had to live through war in my home country, these values have helped me to process difficult experiences and rethink what gives life meaning.
